en: This *Vasudhārā-stotra*, when recited according to the correctly prescribed rites,
bestows abundant prosperity and the enjoyments of the Sugata.
With devotion, I perpetually pay homage to that dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā, whose singular intention is the welfare of all sentient beings. || 1 ||
That which, when remembered, pacifies for men the long-standing, intensely increased suffering of poverty and the misfortune of sin—
that [meditation] known as Vasudhārā, which is like a wish-fulfilling tree— [I praise].
I bow my head constantly for the welfare of all worlds. || 2 ||
The mine of jewels, the treasury of jewel-treasures,
possessing various jewels and raining down reflections; the necklace of jewels, made of jewels, and manifoldly variegated.
And I bow to the Noble One, the stream that sustains the earth. || 3 ||
She, whose hands were fruitful with jewels, illuminated that [place] as she bore the crest-jewel of fame adorned by her generosity;
her limbs were graced by necklaces, half-necklaces, and swaying earrings.
I bow to Māryā, the showerer of wealth, the worthy refuge.
The Vasudhārā Stotra, extracted from the Śrīvasudhārākalpa, is complete.
